The petition is filed by the petitioner U/Sec-22 of Employees Compensation Act, 1923 seeking
compensation for accidental injuries.

1 2. Petitioner case is as Follows:
Petitioner is the driver with the respondent No.2 who is the owner of the Tempo traveler bearing Reg No.KA-06-AB-9701 and he has insured his vehicle with respondent No.1.

That on 29.06.2024 at about 12.45 AM., as per the direction of respondent No.2,
petitioner was driving the vehicle bearing Reg No.KA-063-AB-9701 in outer ring road, when he came near Vishal Mart and he lost his control over the vehicle and dashed to the Lorry from the behind.

In the accident, he sustained grievous injuries,
and jurisdictional police have registered Cr.No.132/2024.
Further petitioner took treatment at Vijayanagara and Sanjay Gandhi Hospital and he has spent Rs.1,00,000/- for his medical expenses.

Petitioner stated that respondent No.2 being his master/ employer he was paying salary of Rs.30,000/- per month and Rs.3,00/- per day as batta and the alleged accident had occurred during and in the course of his employment with the respondent No.2, accordingly respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount with interest and prays this tribunal allowing the petition.
3. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, respondent No.2 has not chosen to contest the petition and he placed exparte.
Respondent No.1 appeared through their counsel, filed vakalath and written statement.
They admitted the issuance of policy to the vehicle belongs to the respondent No.2 and he contended that insured has violated the policy conditions and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.
4. Petitioner examined himself as PW-1, MRO as PW-2 and doctor as PW-3 and his employer as PW-4 produced and marked 22 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 22 and they are fully cross examined.
5. Respondent no.1 examined its official as RW-1, produced and marked 3 documents which are at Ex.D1 to 3 and he is fully cross examined.
6. I have heard the arguments from the counsels appearing for both the sides and perused the entire records.

7. On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following :
ISSUES 1. Whether the claimant proves that he was Workman as per section 2(i)(n) of the Workmen Compensation Act 1923?

2

sentences.text: 2. Whether claimant proves that he has sustained grievous injuries during and in the course of his employment with respondent No.2?
3. Whether respondent No.1 proves that insured has violated the policy conditions?
4. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
if so, what is the quantum and from whom?
5 . What order or award?

8. After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
Issue no.1& 2: In the affirmative, Issue no.3: In the Negative Issue no.4: In Partly Affirmative Issue No.5: As per final order for the following:
REASONS 9. Issue No.1 to 4 :- I have taken these issued together for common discussion, so as to avoid repetition of facts and reasonings:
PW1 being the petitioner, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.

Petitioner has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, Mahazar, sketch, IMV report, final report, police intimation, MLC register which are at Ex.P.1 to 5, 14, 15.
10.

On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents it is evident that petitioner was the driver of Tempo traveler bearing Reg No.KA-06-AB-9701 and he was working with the respondent No.2 and the accident occurred during and in the course of his employment with the respondent no.2, in the cross examination of employer that is PW-4 he clearly deposed that the petitioner was his employee and he was driving the vehicle as on the date of the accident.
It is true that no person will handover the vehicle to the driver unless there exist a relationship of employer and employee between them.
Petitioner has tendered his DL as per Ex.C1 and it is valid as on the date of the accident.

In the cross examination PW-1 & 4, nothing is elicited to disprove the fact that the petitioner was not the employee with respondent No.2 and he sustained grievous injuries during course of his employment with the respondent No.2.
Respondent NO.1 has failed to probabilise their contention as contended in the written statement.
11. Petitioner has tendered the wound certificate, discharge summary, out patient record, as per Ex.P.6, 7, 11, 12 & 16.

The entry therein reveals that petitioner sustained grievous injuries that is contused lacerated wound on his chin, lip, tongue and displacement of inner face of lower anterior teeth and he has spent Rs.47,464/- for his medical expenses as per Ex.P.9.
As per section 4 of the Employees compensation act, actual medical expenses shall be reimbursed.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for Rs.47,464/-.

3 12.

sentences.text: The petitioner has examined the maxillary surgeon as PW-3.
He deposed that, he has not treated the petitioner and he has verified the medical records, wound certificate, inpatient record, discharge summary and he has physically examined the petitioner.
He deposed that petitioner has 13% of whole body disability as per Ex.P17.
Learned advocate for the respondents argued that the assessment of PW-3 is on higher side.

I have perused the evidence of PW-3 wound certificate,
discharge summary given from the hospital, X-ray etc.
13.
Evidently petitioner has not examined the doctor who treated him in both the hospital.

It is true that petitioner sustained grievous injuries that is contused lacerated wound on his chin, lip, tongue and displacement of inner face of lower anterior teeth, the oral testimony of PW-3, corroborates with Ex.P.17 & 18.
Considering the medical reports and oral testimony of doctor, the whole body disability of the petitioner is assessed as 11%.
14. Petitioner has not substantiated his income, accordingly the notional income for the year 2024 that is Rs.16,500/- has to be taken as income of the petitioner.
As per section 4(1)(b) of the Employees Compensation Act, 60% of the monthly income should be multiplied by the relevant factor and by percentage of the disability.
15. The age of petitioner as on the date of accident is 36 years, 11 months & 21 days as per the entry in Aadhar card which is at Ex P.8.
As per schedule IV of the Employee compensation Act 1982, the relevant factor applicable is 192.14.

Accordingly the disability of the petitioner is calculated as follows:
16.
Monthly income Rs.16,500/-, 60% of the monthly salary is Rs.9,900/-X 192.14 relevant factor X11% disability =Rs.2,09,240/-.

In total petitioner is entitled for the following compensation amount 1 Medical expenses Rs.47,464/-
2 Loss of income Rs.2,09,240/-
17. Rate of Interest:

As per statutory mandate in Sec.4A(3)(a) of employees compensation Act 1923,
12% simple rate of interest should be awarded, Accordingly I award the simple interest at the rate of 12% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of accident till its realization.
18. Liability:

The insurance company has not disputed the validity of the policy of the offending vehicle and they have failed to establish their contention that insured has violated the policy conditions and accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner.

Accordingly Respondent No.1 is the liable to pay the compensation amount and respondent No.1 is directed to deposit compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of this order.

Hence with the aforesaid discussion based on the evidence placed on record, Accordingly I am answering Issues No.1 & 2 in the affirmative, Issue No.3 in the negative, Issue No.4 in partly affirmative.

For the foregoing reason and discussion, on the aforesaid issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec-22 of Employees Compensation Act, 1923, is partly allowed with cost.
Petitioner is entitled for the compensation amount of Rs.2,56,704/- with simple interest at the rate of 12% P.A from the date of accident till its realization.
Respondent no.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this tribunal with in 30 days from the date of the judgment.

After depositing the compensation amount with interest, cash shirestedar is directed to release the entire amount with interest to the petitioner, through K2, after compliance of mandate of circular No.39/2020 dated 17.01.2020.
Advocate fee of Rs.1000/- is fixed.
All the interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
Draw award accordingly.
